_comment: Single source of truth for every cross-module constant.
Before this file existed, the ML module and the Decision-Support module each
carried their own copy of the unit rates, the cooling assumptions and the
land-cover mapping. They happened to agree numerically (ML expressed a rate
as inr_per_m2 x coverage_fraction, Decision-Support pre-multiplied the two
into a single effective rate), but nothing enforced that and nothing would
have caught them drifting apart. Both modules now read this file.
Effective per-m2 rate = inr_per_m2 * coverage_fraction:
Tree cover  150 x 0.25 = 37.5
Cool roof   400 x 0.15 = 60.0
Green park  250 x 0.10 = 25.0
These match the rates Decision-Support previously hardcoded.
The four action labels are a hard contract with the dashboard.
frontend/js/config.js keys INTERVENTIONS on these exact strings and
Machine Learning & Prediction/scripts/export_grid_geojson.py enforces
them in VALID_ACTIONS. Do not rename one side only.
coverage_fraction is the share of a ~8,916 m2 cell actually treated.
Treating 100% of a cell is not physically realistic.
cooling_c is a PLANNING ASSUMPTION, not a measurement. The figures
originate in the Decision-Support catalogue, which labels them
'placeholder engineering estimates for a hackathon demo'. Nothing here
is fitted to Guwahati, validated against a field trial, or adjusted for
canopy age, albedo, humidity or wind. Replace before any figure here is
quoted as an outcome.
RATE PROVENANCE -- read before quoting any cost.
Exactly ONE of the three rates below has a real-world comparable behind
it. Do not read the other two as validated.
Green park, 1150 INR/m2 -- SOURCED, revised 2026-08-14 from 250.
Anchored on Gujarat AMRUT 2.0 municipal garden projects: Bhavani
Garden, Lathi, Rs 1.26 crore over 10,936.35 m2 = Rs 1,152/m2; Kailash
Vatika, Palanpur, Rs 2.25 crore over 10,000 m2 = Rs 2,250/m2.
Anchored on the LOWER figure deliberately. Those are ~10,000 m2 civic
gardens including paths, lighting, benches and boundary walls, whereas
this action treats ~892 m2 of soft landscaping. The scope mismatch cuts
both ways (no amenities, but also no economies of scale), so the low
anchor is the defensible end of a 1,150-2,250 INR/m2 range.
The previous 250 INR/m2 was roughly 5-9x below every real comparable,
and because cost drives the cooling-per-rupee ranking it made parks
look like the most cost-effective intervention available. They are not.
Tree cover, 150 INR/m2 -- UNCHANGED, STILL AN ASSUMPTION.
Works out to ~3,750 INR per tree at one tree per 25 m2 of treated area.
Bulk plantation in India runs 200-500 INR/tree including three years of
care, but that is rural bulk planting and is NOT a comparable: urban
municipal planting adds pit excavation, a tree guard, staking, soil
replacement and tanker watering. No directly comparable urban municipal
rate was found, so this figure stands unvalidated.
Cool roof, 400 INR/m2 -- UNCHANGED, STILL AN ASSUMPTION.
Sits between two non-comparable scopes: high-SRI coating materials
retail around 173 INR/m2 (10 kg covering 400 sq ft at Rs 6,400), while
quoted professional application services run 90-140 INR/sq ft
(970-1,510 INR/m2) but include waterproofing this action does not.
Neither bounds a coating-only municipal programme, so this figure also
stands unvalidated.
ESA WorldCover v200 class codes, as exported by the GEE script into the
LandCover column of dataset.csv.
KNOWN LIMITATION: WorldCover has no dedicated road class - roads fall
into the generic built_up category alongside buildings. The suitability
rules below are defensive about this: built_up cells are only ever
assigned roof-type interventions, which are moot rather than harmful if
a given built_up cell turns out to be a road. Ground-level interventions
are never placed on built_up.
Heat_Risk quantile cut points. Quantiles rather than absolute cutoffs
because Heat_Risk is a unit-scaled composite whose absolute value is not
physically meaningful across cities - the tiers are relative ranks
within Guwahati.
